sets.title: Italy and Germany
sets.docs: Casefile C (10.2), Documents 5 and 6: Cavour, 1846; Bismarck, 1862

tasks.prompt: Name the parts. Drag each sentence to its job (or tap the sentence, then tap the job).

pieces.text: In the 1800s, Italy and Germany were split into many small states, and leaders worked to unite each one into a single nation.
An enduring issue these documents raise is nationalism. Nationalism is when a people's loyalty to their own nation becomes a push for that nation to rule itself.
Document 6 shows this when Bismarck says the goal will be achieved “by blood and iron.”
Outside the documents, I know that in 1871 Prussia's king was proclaimed kaiser of a new German Empire.

hints: Which sentence sets the scene before anything else?
Which one is true but isn't in either document?
tasks.reasoning: Context sets the scene, the issue is named and explained, evidence comes from a document, and outside evidence comes from what you know.

distractors.CONTEXT: That sentence does more than set the scene. Look for the one that tells when and what was happening.
distractors.ISSUE: Look for the sentence that names the issue and says what it means.
distractors.EVIDENCE: Evidence names a document and pulls a detail from it.
distractors.OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Outside evidence is true and isn't in the documents. Is that one in a document?

pieces.text: In the 1800s, Italy and Germany were split into many small states, and leaders worked to unite each one into a single nation.
An enduring issue these documents raise is nationalism. Nationalism is when a people's loyalty to their own nation becomes a push for that nation to rule itself.
Document 5 shows this when Cavour says “all the petty questions that divide us must be silenced” so Italy can unite.
Document 6 shows it too, when Bismarck says the goal will be achieved “by blood and iron.”
This issue matters because the same force that built Italy and Germany out of small states could also break apart empires that ruled many peoples.

paragraph: In the 1800s, Italy and Germany were split into many small states, and leaders worked to unite each one into a single nation.
An enduring issue these documents raise is nationalism. Nationalism is when a people's loyalty to their own nation becomes a push for that nation to rule itself.
Document 6 shows this when Bismarck says the goal will be achieved “by blood and iron.”
This issue matters because the same force that built Italy and Germany out of small states could also break apart empires that ruled many peoples.

pieces.text: This shows that for Bismarck, a united Germany would come from war, not from votes or speeches.
Outside the documents, I know that in 1871 Prussia's king was proclaimed kaiser of a new German Empire.
Cavour wanted Italy to be glorious and powerful.
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain.

hints: The explanation says what the evidence right before it shows. Look for “This shows…”
Outside evidence is true, isn't in Documents 5 or 6, and connects to the issue.
tasks.reasoning: The explanation says what Bismarck's words mean; the outside fact shows where his way led. That's evidence put to work.

distractors.j3: That's in Document 5, so it's document evidence, not outside evidence, and it doesn't explain Bismarck's words.
distractors.j4: True, but it doesn't connect to nationalism in these documents. Outside evidence has to fit.
distractors.swap: Both pieces belong, just in each other's spot. Which one explains, and which one brings in something new?

sets.title: Empires coming apart
sets.docs: Casefile C (10.2), Documents 7 and 8: the peoples of Austria-Hungary, 1911; “The Boiling Point,” Punch, 1912

tasks.prompt: Name the parts. Drag each sentence to its job (or tap the sentence, then tap the job).

An enduring issue these documents raise is conflict. Conflict is when groups, nations or ideas struggle against each other, from argument to war.
Document 8 shows this when the great powers of Europe sit on the lid of a pot labeled “Balkan Troubles.”
Outside the documents, I know that in 1914 a Bosnian Serb nationalist shot the heir to Austria-Hungary's throne, and Europe went to war.
